subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin stopped counting days and started counting how much his boots hurt.
source_quote: We'd been on the road south out of the Silver Marches long enough that I'd stopped counting days and started counting how much my boots hurt.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin keeps noting that the surface had given them back the sky, and he keeps meaning it.
source_quote: The surface had given us back the sky — I keep noting this, and I keep meaning it —

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the unnatural silence in Daggerford, like the one from his childhood village.
source_quote: The hill giants I grew up with — they had a word for a silence that wasn't natural.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin watched a woman cross the road to avoid a conversation and then pretend she hadn't.
source_quote: I watched a woman cross the road to avoid a conversation and then pretend she hadn't.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin stared at the bronze forearm monument longer than he should have.
source_quote: I stared at it for longer than I should have.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to make sure he hadn't misread the Dwarven inscription because it was one of his languages.
source_quote: I read it twice because Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought about how many towns north of Daggerford had similar stories but hadn't put up monuments.
source_quote: I stood in the doorway of the River Shining and thought about how many towns north of here had a story like this, and just hadn't put up a bronze arm about it yet.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the unnatural silence in Daggerford but didn't say anything.
source_quote: Grygum noticed it too, I could tell, though he didn't say anything.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum made a noise when he read that Tarvis Ulain had served Bahamut, signaling something clicked into place.
source_quote: Grygum made a sound when he got to the part confirming Tarvis had served Bahamut — not a word, just the noise a person makes when something clicks into place.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was quiet in a way he wasn't usually, because he was adding something to his list.
source_quote: Grygum was quiet. Not the usual quiet. The kind where he's adding something to the list.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum dropped a gold piece for the pewter hand cast because he had leverage after paying.
source_quote: Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled Stool when thinking about Elin’s silence, recognizing silence as not absence.
source_quote: I thought about Stool. I couldn't help it. A creature that communicated through spores and rapport rather than words, who nonetheless had more to say than most creatures I'd met with full use of their tongues.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Elin’s silence was insistence, not absence, because she was trying to say something.
source_quote: Silence isn't absence. Seven years old and drawing the same thing on every flat surface is not nothing — it's insistence.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum wrote down Elin’s words 'The wells are not wells anymore' because something in her voice was doing work the words weren't.
source_quote: I wrote it down. It is what I do. But I held it for a moment first. Something in the voice was doing work the words weren't.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought about Zuggtmoy when considering fungal infection as a cause for Elin’s condition.
source_quote: I asked about fungal involvement specifically, because I still think about Zuggtmoy, and will probably continue thinking about Zuggtmoy for the rest of my life.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the madness from the Underdark was reaching the surface and affecting Elin.
source_quote: The madness from the Underdark — the deep, structural wrongness we'd felt building around the demon lords... was not, apparently, staying below. It was reaching up. It was reaching Elin.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that Elin’s condition was not a disease but a breakdown in how the world reached her.
source_quote: It wasn't a disease in the conventional sense. It was more like the world had started speaking a language she couldn't process...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized Daz’s headache might be connected to Elin’s condition, though the link was tenuous.
source_quote: I sat with that question long enough to actually examine it properly. 'Does it seem related at all to how the other person was hearing voices?' Twenty-three. My best of the evening, arriving too late to be medically useful and just in time to be philosophically concerning.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum filed the connection between Elin and Daz under open questions and kept writing.
source_quote: I filed it under open questions and kept writing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to wear armor, though it is not directly stated, his actions imply resistance to conventional protection.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the pressure in his own head, which he had been mentioning indirectly for a while.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the wall at the Burning Wizard Inn remembers the wizard who was burned alive.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz catalogued the exits at the Burning Wizard Inn with precision.
source_quote: I noted the exits. Front door, obvious. Side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels. Stairs to the upper rooms. The window behind the performer's corner, narrow but workable in an emergency.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz found Whistler’s restraint in taking only what was needed from Tiamat’s hoard genuinely impressive.
source_quote: I found that, I mean, genuinely impressive. The restraint of it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir looked at the bronze forearm monument like he was deciding whether it constituted a threat.
source_quote: Zalthir looked at it the way he looks at most things: like he was deciding whether it constituted a threat.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir articulated that Elin’s hallucinations were not magic but a deeper failure of perception.
source_quote: Zalthir articulated the mechanism: the input, the audio, the way the world was arriving at her rather than the world itself.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir produced an alarm as professional commentary on the situation with Elin.
source_quote: Zalthir produced an alarm from somewhere, which I took as professional commentary.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel personally signed off on the Tarvis Ulain monument as head of the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Maerith
fact: Maerith had the exhaustion of someone who had been turned away by every temple that was supposed to help.
source_quote: Maerith of the Ford had the look of a woman who had already been turned away. You develop an eye for it, in this work — the specific exhaustion of someone who has walked into every room that was supposed to help and left each one carrying the same weight back out.

subject: Maerith
fact: Maerith said yes to every question asked about her daughter Elin’s condition.
source_quote: She didn't say no to anything, in her own telling. She said yes.

subject: Festrum
fact: Festrum believes the wall at the Burning Wizard Inn remembers the wizard who was burned alive.
source_quote: My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: The Stroudite inscription on Tarvis’s monument
fact: Someone placed a Stroudite inscription on a Bahamutian paladin’s monument, and no one removed it because it was a gift.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild... we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?

subject: The wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s first words after restoration were 'The wells are not wells anymore,' a sentence that means more than it says.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: The six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin draws the same six-pointed star on every flat surface as an act of insistence, not madness.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface.
